_comment: Per-APPLICATION outcome library for the MeridianCore servicing product.
These are attached to every capability recorded against this vendor product,
because they are properties of the application rather than of any one flow:
every screen in MeridianCore can return 'no such member', expire a session,
or deny on entitlement. Recording them per-capability would mean rediscovering
the same six facts for every flow, and a happy-path discovery run never
observes any of them anyway.
Splitting them this way is also what makes them reviewable. The business
outcomes are part of a capability's public contract -- a calling agent has to
handle 'member_not_found' -- so they need a human to have written them down
deliberately, not a model to have guessed them from one run.
Detection strings are the exact operator-facing wording. That is a real
coupling and it is the right one: these strings are the only thing the
application gives us to distinguish 'the record does not exist' from 'the
automation broke'. Per-tenant rewording is handled by the `labels` override
(see config/tenants.json), and a string that stops matching surfaces as a
hard failure rather than a silent misclassification.

business_outcomes.name: member_not_found
business_outcomes.description: No member exists with the supplied number. A legitimate answer, not a failure.

detect.value: No member matching that number was found
detect.description: the search screen reports an empty result

business_outcomes.name: member_restricted
business_outcomes.description: The member profile is restricted; servicing actions are unavailable for it.

detect.description: the member record shows a restriction notice

business_outcomes.name: not_authorized
business_outcomes.description: The signed-in operator lacks the entitlement for this action. The caller should route to a supervisor.

detect.value: You are not authorized to open sub-accounts
detect.description: the application refused on entitlement grounds

business_outcomes.name: deposit_limit_exceeded
business_outcomes.description: The requested opening deposit is above the branch limit and needs supervisor approval.

detect.description: inline validation error on the sub-account form

business_outcomes.name: invalid_deposit_amount
business_outcomes.description: The supplied deposit amount was not a valid monetary value.

detect.value: Initial deposit must be a numeric amount
detect.description: inline validation error on the sub-account form
the sign-in screen refused the credentials

recovery_rules.name: dismiss_maintenance_notice
recovery_rules.description: A scheduled-maintenance interstitial can appear on any screen. Acknowledge it and carry on.

detect.description: the maintenance interstitial is covering the working area

locator.description: the Acknowledge link on the maintenance notice

recovery_rules.name: reauthenticate_on_session_expiry
recovery_rules.description: The session can expire mid-flow. Re-run the sign-in steps and resume where we left off.

detect.description: the application bounced us back to the sign-in screen

_comment: Re-execute the steps from here up to (not including) the one that was
interrupted, then retry it. '@first' means the whole prefix, which for
this app re-runs sign-in and re-navigates to the record.
The executor REFUSES this recovery if any step in the prefix is
irreversible, and escalates instead. Silently replaying a prefix that
contains a commit would post the transaction twice -- a recovery
mechanism must never be able to cause the thing it is recovering from.

recovery_rules.name: retry_transient_slow_load
recovery_rules.description: The application is intermittently slow. Wait and re-attempt the step before calling it a failure.

detect.description: engaged when the surface times out, not by anything visible on screen
